title: Layers 2 and 6 measured on real tables: more rows (holds), retrain (needs work)
request: The owner, 2026-10-25: more ability for the students beyond leakage; each layer's rule measured on real tables, its decision fixed before any result.
spec: PLAN.md beside each measurement (agent_runs/live_tests/2026-10-25-more-rows-truth, -retrain-truth), written before any result.
plan: Double the rows of each real table and see whether the learning curve's answer came true.
Replay the champion/challenger rule along each time-ordered table and see the future of every promotion and every kept champion.

decisions.decision: A rule found 'needs work' is not changed tonight.
decisions.why: A change is its own package, its rule fixed and confirmed on other tables first, as the threshold change was (and failed).

change: No product code: measurements, evidence ABL-003 and ABL-004, measured labels (94 records) in each measurement's ledger.

measurements.name: ABL-003 more rows
measurements.gate: the rule holds if likely_help and unlikely_help each come true on most tables and are rarely proved wrong (PLAN.md)
measurements.result: 58 tables: likely_help came true on 17 of 19, unlikely_help on 16 of 19 (2 proved wrong); cannot_tell on 34% of the tables, of which 15 of 20 gained
measurements.next: cannot_tell is often a gain: a student could learn where the curve is too careful

measurements.name: ABL-004 retrain
measurements.gate: needs work if more than 10% of promotions are worse in the future, or more than 50% of the kept champions had a better challenger
measurements.result: 13 tables, 36 decisions: 2 of 27 promotions worse in the future (7.4%); 5 of 9 kept champions had a better challenger (55.6%)
measurements.next: a less careful promotion rule as its own package, fixed before it is measured, confirmed on other time-ordered tables

outcome: The more-rows rule stands as it is; the retrain rule keeps too many champions and is named for its own package.
lessons: A cautious rule looks safe on its 'yes' answers; its 'no' and 'cannot tell' answers are where its cost hides.
